about: India's tunnel boring machines: the October 2026 announcement that India is building its own, the Chinese export controls behind it, and every machine reported at work in India. Each figure is quoted from the report it came from; where reports disagree, both are given.

claims.claim: India now manufactures tunnel boring machines of 8 m and 15 m diameter, after relying on imports.
claims.quote: India, which previously relied on imports to meet its TBM requirements, is now manufacturing machines with diameters of 8 metres and 15 metres.
claims.check: The 15 m class matches a named machine: Herrenknecht's Chennai plant is building two 15.62 m Mixshields for Mumbai's Versova–Dahisar Link Road — with core components from Schwanau, Germany. 'Manufactured in India' here means built and assembled in India by a foreign maker, not designed by an Indian one.

claims.claim: India is preparing to build machines larger than 16 m in diameter.
claims.quote: The country is also preparing to manufacture TBMs with diameters exceeding 16 metres.
claims.check: A target, not a machine. One outlet (HelloRail) wrote that India is already capable of building 16 m+ machines; no other report says so, and no 16 m+ order in India is named in any report found.

claims.claim: The aim is a full ecosystem — design, manufacture and maintenance — with Tamil Nadu as its base.
claims.quote: The ecosystem aims to cover every stage of the process, from design and manufacturing to maintenance.
claims.check: Of the three, design is the stage with least to show: BEML's 2025 calls were for a foreign design consultant and a technology partner, and no selected partner has been reported.

claims.claim: Tunnel boring machines have been used in the Himalayas on the Rishikesh–Karnaprayag line.
claims.quote: TBMs have been deployed for tunnelling work through the difficult Himalayan terrain on the Rishikesh-Karnaprayag line.
claims.check: Confirmed by L&T: TBM 'Shakti', 9.11 m, bored 10.4 km of the 14.57 km Tunnel No. 8 and broke through in April 2025. Herrenknecht separately reports supplying the project's two single-shield machines; neither release says whether Shakti is one of them.

claims.claim: A $1.2 billion, seven-year incentive scheme for high-value construction machinery, including TBMs.
claims.quote: India is preparing to approve a $1.2 billion incentive programme aimed at boosting domestic production of high-value construction and infrastructure equipment.
claims.check: Reported, not notified. No approval had been reported by the last search; the heavy industries and finance ministries did not comment.

controls.by: China's Ministry of Commerce and General Administration of Customs
controls.covers: Full-face tunnel boring machines and parts specially designed for them, along with walking excavators and plateau-type wet shotcrete machines.
controls.licence: Exporters shipping to 'sensitive countries and regions' must apply for a licence; others register for an export certificate. The notice names no country.
controls.threshold: No diameter threshold for TBMs was found in the reporting; the size cut-offs reported apply to dredger parts.
controls.quote: Exporters to sensitive countries shall apply for a license from the competent department of commerce under the State Council.

machines.name: Two Mixshields (unnamed)
machines.project: Versova–Dahisar Link Road, Mumbai — tunnel packages C and D, 3.1 km each
machines.builtIn: Chennai, India, with core components from Schwanau, Germany
machines.status: Ordered December 2024; largest TBMs ordered for India
machines.quote: The German family-owned company will supply two Mixshields, each with a diameter of 15,620 mm.

machines.name: Three Mixshields
machines.project: Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train: 16 km of the 21 km Mumbai tunnel, 7 km of it under Thane Creek
machines.builtIn: Guangzhou, China (Swarajya); an earlier report said Chennai — the more detailed and recent account says Guangzhou
machines.status: First launched at Vikhroli on 5 July 2026; second from Sawli (Ghansoli) on 18 July 2026. Held at Chinese ports from 2024; unloaded at Mumbai's JNPT on 23 March 2026
machines.quote: The slurry-based Mixshield TBM features a 13.6-m-diameter cutterhead, weighs 3,200 tonnes and is 96 m long.
machines.notes: Weight is reported as 3,000 t (Free Press Journal) and 3,200 t (Equipment India).

machines.name: Nayak and Arjuna
machines.project: Thane–Borivali Twin Tunnel, Mumbai — 10.25 km of twin tunnels in an 11.84 km project
machines.builtIn: Chennai, India, with core components from Germany
machines.status: Nayak launched 7 April 2026; Arjuna launched 13 August 2026
machines.quote: Herrenknecht AG supplied the machine through its Indian manufacturing facility in Chennai, with core components sourced from its primary production base in Germany.

machines.name: Shakti, and a second machine
machines.project: Rishikesh–Karnaprayag rail line, Tunnel No. 8 (14.57 km), Uttarakhand
machines.maker: L&T (contractor, client RVNL); Herrenknecht reports supplying the project's two single-shield machines
machines.builtIn: Not stated in the reports found
machines.status: Broke through April 2025, the first TBM drive on Indian mountain rail; 10.4 km bored at an average 413 m a month
machines.quote: The breakthrough was achieved using a state-of-the-art Single-Shield Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) named Shakti, of 9.11m diameter, which is also the largest TBM to be deployed in the Himalayan region.
machines.notes: L&T names Shakti; Herrenknecht describes two machines on a 10.5 km twin-tube section. Whether Shakti is one of those two is not stated in either release.

machines.name: Durga (S-1410A) and Divya (S-1411A)
machines.builtIn: Alinjivakkam, Tamil Nadu; cutterhead, manlock, material lock and propulsion sourced from outside India
machines.status: Durga broke through 10 July 2026; Divya at Victoria in August 2026 after a 1.72 km drive
machines.quote: Some critical components, such as the cutter head, manlock, material lock and propulsion system, were sourced externally, while most of the two TBMs were built indigenously.
machines.notes: Weight is reported as 650 t (NBM&CW) and about 600 t (the ministry, as quoted).

machines.name: Fifteen or more, in three corridors
machines.project: Chennai Metro Phase 2 — seven on Corridor 3's first 9 km, four on Corridor 4, four on Corridor 5
machines.builtIn: Not stated in the reports found
machines.status: 24 breakthroughs by August 2026; Marutham broke through at Villivakkam on 1 October 2026
machines.quote: Four TBMs with an excavated diameter of 6.67 m are being used to build about 16 km of twin tunnels on this corridor.
machines.notes: No single report gives the Phase 2 total; 15 is the sum of the three corridor counts reported, a floor rather than a count. 6.67 m is Corridor 4's figure.

machines.name: Narmada and three more
machines.project: Indore Metro Yellow Line, Airport–Bada Ganpati
machines.builtIn: Not stated in the reports found
machines.quote: TERRATEC says four EPB machines are headed to the Indore Yellow Line, with two shipping first.

machines.name: First TBM
machines.status: Lowered to about 24 m; tunnelling began late March 2026
machines.quote: Bhopal Metro project enters new phase as underground tunnel construction work begins.

machines.name: Phase 4 fleet
machines.project: Delhi Metro Phase 4 — 40.1 km of underground line planned
machines.status: Aerocity–Tughlakabad (19.34 km underground) tunnelling complete; for scale, Phase 3 used about 30 TBMs for about 50 km
machines.quote: In Phase-3, when approximately 50 kilometres of underground sections were built, about 30 TBMs were deployed in the national capital.

makers.name: Herrenknecht India, Chennai
makers.what: Described as the only dedicated TBM assembly plant in India: the company says it covers 10 acres, with a cutter workshop, steel-construction bays for shields and cutterheads, and welding and machining lines. It builds and assembles machines with core components from Germany; most of the company's large machines are still built in Guangzhou, China.

makers.name: BEML (state-owned, Bengaluru)
makers.what: Called in July 2025 for a design consultant and in September 2025 for a technology partner, to design TBMs from about 6 m to 16.5 m; reported to start with a 6.5 m machine, possibly with Delhi Metro. Signed a broader metro MoU with DMRC on 8 April 2026. No partner selection reported.

makers.name: Larsen & Toubro
makers.what: Contractor on the Rishikesh–Karnaprayag Tunnel No. 8 and Kolkata's Line 3 drives, and named by Reuters as a likely beneficiary of the incentive scheme. It runs TBMs; no report found says it builds them.

parts.name: Cutterhead
parts.does: The rotating face. Steel disc cutters roll against rock and crack it; scrapers lift soft ground into the chamber behind.
parts.india: Chennai fabricates cutterhead steelwork and makes cutting tools; the Kolkata machines' cutterheads were sourced from outside India.

parts.name: Main drive and bearing
parts.does: Electric motors turn the cutterhead through the main bearing — the part that carries the cutterhead's load and largely decides how long the machine can work.
parts.india: Among the 'core components' reported to come from Herrenknecht's German base for the Chennai-built machines.

parts.name: Shield
parts.does: A steel cylinder that holds the ground up while the machine digs, and keeps the crew and machinery inside it safe.
parts.india: Chennai has steel-construction bays for shields.

parts.name: Thrust cylinders
parts.does: Hydraulic rams push against the last ring of tunnel lining to drive the machine forward, one ring's length at a time.
parts.india: Kolkata's 'propulsion system' was sourced from outside India.

parts.name: Segment erector
parts.does: A robot arm that picks up concrete segments and bolts them into a ring behind the shield — the tunnel's permanent wall.
parts.india: No report found says where it is made.

parts.name: Screw conveyor or slurry circuit
parts.does: Carries excavated ground out of the chamber: a screw in earth-pressure machines, pumped slurry in Mixshields.
parts.india: No report found says where it is made.

parts.name: Back-up gantries
parts.does: A train of trailers behind the shield carrying power, pumps, grout, ventilation and the control cabin — most of the length of a machine that, for the bullet-train TBMs, runs to 96 m.
parts.india: Chennai assembles complete machines in modules.

timeline.what: India's commerce minister tells Germany's vice-chancellor that China has started blocking Herrenknecht's China-built TBMs bound for India.
TBM Shakti breaks through on Tunnel No. 8, Rishikesh–Karnaprayag: India's longest rail tunnel, and the first TBM drive in the Himalayas.
BEML calls for a design consultant to develop Indian TBMs.
China is reported to lift curbs on fertiliser, rare earths and TBMs bound for India; Business Today says it could not verify the report.
BEML calls for a TBM technology partner.
Two Herrenknecht machines for the bullet train, each over 13 m wide and 2,000 t, are unloaded at JNPT, Mumbai, after being held in China.
Nayak, 13.34 m, India's largest hard-rock TBM, is launched on the Thane–Borivali twin tunnel.
BEML and Delhi Metro sign an MoU; Delhi Metro's managing director stresses Indian design and production of TBMs.
The first bullet-train TBM starts its 6 km drive from Vikhroli to BKC.
The second starts under Thane Creek — India's first undersea rail tunnel.
Arjuna, the second Thane–Borivali TBM, is launched.
Reuters reports a $1.2 billion, seven-year incentive scheme for TBMs and other heavy equipment is close to approval.
China announces export controls on TBMs and their parts, to take effect on 18 November.
Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw says India now makes 8 m and 15 m TBMs and is preparing to build machines over 16 m.
China's TBM export controls take effect.

trade.label: India's imports of tunnelling machinery from China, US$ million
trade.quote: Chinese-sourced tunnelling machinery imports fell from USD 18 million in FY23 to USD 3 million in FY24 and USD 500,000 in FY25, before rising to USD 800,000 in FY26.
trade.caveat: These are small sums beside the 2,000-tonne-plus machines on this page, and the reporting does not name the trade code, so read them as one customs line and not as India's dependence on China. Outlook found that official material establishes no precise share of India's TBM imports sourced from China; Takshashila put dependence on China for standard TBMs at almost 100% in 2019, by its own trade classification.
